submission.natural_language_explanation: Fires on a common count noun that names a countable unit of organised life -- an instance, quantity, group, service, role, product or measurement that a business, clinic, study or public body counts, records, provides or reports (cases, samples, rates, results, costs, prices, benefits, risks, services, programs, facilities, populations, patients, staff, products, treatments, symptoms, tests, hospitals, orders, shipments). It stays near zero on everyday objects, foods, clothing, body parts and household items (apple, dog, cliff, river, bread, shirt, hand, cup), on emotion and abstract-universal words (hope, truth, freedom, science, history), on generic person words (man, woman, person), and on the same class noun inside a fixed adverbial idiom ('in many cases').

The pole fires on the head of an attributive or compound noun phrase (the second element of 'N N' or 'Adj N', as in 'steel tray', 'cliff face', 'school bus'), regardless of what the noun means, so concrete compound heads should fire and bare institutional nouns should not.

The pole is an abstract-noun or institutional-register feature, so other abstract nouns in report prose ('idea', 'truth', 'memory', 'science', 'history') and concrete nouns inside institutional text should fire as strongly as 'sample' and 'result'.
